description:
Added

  • Memory management — Add node details, Skill memory export, and profile schema listing, inspection, updates and deletion; support rule-scoped recall, pro/lite search, skill metadata and profile-only extraction.
  • Personal memory Skill — Add bailian-memory for consent-based personal memory, recall and user profile workflows.
  • DeepSeek Harness integrations — Add the personal memory plugin with automatic recall, asynchronous curation and remember/forget tools; update the knowledge plugin for dsh 0.2.1 settings and isolated management credentials.

Changed

  • Memory CLI migration (BREAKING) — Memory commands now use a Workspace-specific endpoint. Configure --workspace-id, BAILIAN_WORKSPACE_ID or workspace_id; replace --memory-library-id with --library-id on commands that support it. Remove --user-id from memory update and memory delete; confirmed node deletion now requires --yes.
  • Memory writes (BREAKING) — memory add now submits asynchronous extraction and waits up to 120 seconds by default. Use --wait 0 for submission-only behavior. JSON consumers must handle event_id and events; a submission receipt is not proof of completed extraction.
  • Unified releases — CLI, Knowledge Studio CLI and both dsh plugins now share one version and release workflow. The dsh knowledge plugin moves from its independent 0.1.x series to 2.5.0.

Removed

  • Legacy knowledge retrieval (BREAKING) — Remove bl knowledge retrieve, kscli retrieve and the knowledgeRetrieve command export. Migrate to bl knowledge search or kscli search using a retrieval service's --agent-id; old index-based arguments are not interchangeable.
  • Legacy Memory library API (BREAKING) — Replace the exported MemoryAddResponse type with MemoryAddAsyncResponse; library consumers must adapt to the updated asynchronous request/response contracts.

Fixed

  • Memory completion and input validation — Empty event lists and missing event IDs no longer falsely confirm completion; polling obeys its deadline, partial failures return a non-zero exit code, and malformed JSON elements and attribute types are rejected before requests.
  • Search documentation — Clarify that --min-score defaults to 0.3 and only applies to pro search; lite does not filter by this threshold.

Security

  • Workspace endpoints — Reject Workspace identifiers that could alter the destination host, preventing credentials from being sent to an unintended host.

Fix race creating the JSON file cache directory (#10789)

When several AWS CLI processes start at the same time and the cache
directory (e.g. ~/.aws/cli/cache) does not exist yet, more than one
process can pass the os.path.isdir() check in JSONFileCache.__setitem__
and call os.makedirs(). All but the first then fail with
"[Errno 17] File exists".

Pass exist_ok=True to os.makedirs(), matching the fix already merged in
botocore (boto/botocore@f1c1bc90aa292b42195edecf4cf35ae348e6cc37).

Minor Changes

  • #16363 d3240f2 Thanks @jamesopstad! - Remove the experimental.newConfig option from Vite plugin v1

    Vite plugin v1 now supports Wrangler configuration files only. Projects using cloudflare.config.ts for configuration should upgrade to Vite plugin v2 beta.

Patch Changes

  • #16373 8cc5f87 Thanks @petebacondarwin! - Report unsupported remote bindings under Bun instead of hanging

    Starting remote bindings now fails with an actionable error explaining Bun's unsupported request routing. Use Node.js or disable remote bindings to continue local development.

  • #16334 9cecd09 Thanks @petebacondarwin! - Fix Container setup guidance in Vite development and preview

    Container registry instructions now show the Wrangler command and the configuration location, including Wrangler files and inline Vite configuration.

  • #16333 68d6eec Thanks @petebacondarwin! - Update the local Workers runtime to the October 19 release

    Include the fix for nested asset paths during local development on Windows, together with the compatible Wrangler release.

    The runtime update also disposes Workflow step results and introspection modifiers after use, preventing undisposed RPC warnings and cancelled local Workflow requests.

  • #16379 160e655 Thanks @petebacondarwin! - Update the local Workflow runtime to use native storage cleanup

    Consume the Miniflare fix that queues Workflow persistence deletion with instance recreation, including deletion through the local Explorer. This prevents storage cleanup from racing reuse of the same Workflow instance ID.

  • #16289 bbe822f Thanks @petebacondarwin! - Retry remote preview token refreshes after transient failures

    Backport the retry fix to the private remote-bindings workspace package and require wrangler@4.151.1 so long-running remote development sessions recover after a network outage.

  • #16291 0262f7d Thanks @petebacondarwin! - Use published SDK dependencies for Vite plugin v1 maintenance

    Pin the plugin's published SDK dependencies to their deployed npm versions. Keep private shared packages as workspace dependencies so their implementation and build tools remain available on the v1 maintenance branch.

Patch Changes

  • #15611 4508172 Thanks @taylorlee! - Allow wrangler dev to start module Workers without a default export

    Previously, wrangler dev failed to start module Workers that exported only named entrypoints, such as RPC services, unless an unused default export was added. These Workers now start normally in local development without that workaround.

  • #16370 61fc739 Thanks @WalshyDev! - Fetch the remote config diff from the configured compliance region

    When a Worker was last deployed from the dashboard, wrangler deploy and wrangler versions upload download its remote configuration to compare with the local one. These requests ignored the compliance_region field in the Wrangler configuration file and only honoured the CLOUDFLARE_COMPLIANCE_REGION environment variable. A FedRAMP High Worker configured through the config file would send them to api.cloudflare.com instead of api.fed.cloudflare.com, and the deploy would fail with authentication errors. Rebuild ParseIterator's cached parser when parser options change (#27321)

Running a multi-statement script through `duckdb -c` applies
parser-affecting `SET` statements too late. On current main:

```
$ duckdb -csv -c "SET integer_division=true; SELECT 2/4 AS q"
q
0.5
```

The same two statements through stdin return `0`, as expected:

```
$ printf 'SET integer_division=true;\nSELECT 2/4 AS q;\n' | duckdb -csv
q
0
```

The problem was encountered while exercising grammar extensions through
the CLI, where `SET active_grammar_extensions=[...]` at the start of a
`-c` string did not activate the grammar extension for the rest of the
string. Every setting read by `ClientContext::GetParserOptions` is
affected the same way, including `preserve_identifier_case`,
`max_expression_depth` and `regex_match_operator_semantics`. The
exception is `allow_parser_override_extension`: `parser_override`
extensions are consulted only once per input, guarded by
`override_resolved`, so a `SET` of that setting between statements
intentionally stays outside the scope of this fix.

The shell iterates lazily over a `-c` string. `ExecuteSQL` parses one
statement through a `ParseIterator`, executes it, then parses the next.
`ParseIterator::Peek` re-reads the parser options from the client
context on every call, but the `Parser` instance was kept alive across
calls and constructed exactly once with the options of the first `Peek`.
The freshly read options were silently ignored afterwards, so a `SET`
executed between two statements of the same input never reached the
later statements. Stdin behaves correctly because each line gets a fresh
iterator.

The fix drops the cached `Parser` member. `Peek` constructs a `Parser`
on the stack from the freshly read options for every statement. `Parser`
only holds a copy of the options and a shared pointer to the compiled
grammar, and the matcher caches live in the shared `CompiledGrammar`, so
nothing warm is lost by constructing one per statement. Tokenization is
unaffected, it is grammar-free and the cached token stream stays valid,
consistent with the existing comment in `EnsureTokenized`. Rerunning the
tokenizer when a `DialectExtension` changes the tokenizer mid input is
left to a follow-up, as discussed in the review.

With the fix:

```
$ duckdb -csv -c "SET integer_division=true; SELECT 2/4 AS q"
q
0
```

Two shell tests pin the behavior, one for `integer_division` and one for
`preserve_identifier_case` (an unquoted alias that must come out
lowercased because of the `SET` in front of it). A C++ test covers the
same mechanism through `Connection::Query` with a multi-statement
string, the code path that also serves the C API v2 statement iterator.
A sqllogictest exercises the motivating case directly, with a single
multi-statement string that loads `loadable_grammar_extension_demo`,
activates `pipe_query_syntax` and then runs a pipe query. A companion
negative test checks that the grammar extension stays inactive on a
connection that did not run the `SET`.

description:
Materializing results: wait on NO_TASKS_AVAILABLE like the other execution loops (#27738)

This PR makes the materializing path handle `NO_TASKS_AVAILABLE` the
same way the other execution loops already do.

The loops that drive a query's tasks treat `NO_TASKS_AVAILABLE` (the
remaining tasks are running on other threads) differently:

| loop | on `NO_TASKS_AVAILABLE` |
|---|---|
| `ClientContext::RunToResultStatementInternal` | `WaitForTask` |
| `ResultStreamBase::FetchUnitInternal` (streaming) | `WaitForTask` |
| `QueryResult::CompleteInternal` (materializing) | re-loops at once |
| `ClientContext::CompleteDelegatedInternal` | re-loops at once |

In the two loops that re-loop, the collecting thread spins at 100% CPU
while the workers finish the last pipelines. On every pass it takes
`executor_lock` (in `Executor::IdleState`) and the producer queue lock,
which the workers also need. I couldn't find a reason for
materialization to behave differently from the other paths. It looks
like these two loops were never updated when the others started waiting.

The change adds `NO_TASKS_AVAILABLE` to the wait condition of these two
loops. It is one condition per loop, using the existing `WaitForTask`,
with no new synchronization. If the difference is intentional, I'd like
to understand why. In that case, the numbers below may still help decide
which behavior should be the standard.

**Backport:** I'd suggest backporting this to `v2.0-cyanoptera`. The
change applies there unchanged: these loops and `Executor::WaitForTask`
are identical on both branches, and the measurements below were taken on
`v2.0-cyanoptera`.

### Why no wake-up is missed

`Executor::WaitForTask` returns at once if execution has finished or
errored, or if the producer has a task queued. Otherwise it waits on
`task_reschedule` for at most `WAIT_TIME` (20 ms). Every way the query
can make progress notifies `task_reschedule`:

- New tasks are scheduled at query start, or from inside a running
`ExecutorTask` (`Event::SetTasks`, `AsyncResult::ScheduleTasks`). When
that task is destroyed, `UnregisterTask` calls `notify_all` under
`executor_lock`.
- A descheduled task is woken through `RescheduleTask`.
- An interrupt fails the running tasks, so the same notify fires, and
`WaitForTask` returns at once because the executor now has an error.

In practice, none of 80k short queries took more than 15 ms with the
patch.

### Results

48-core aarch64 machine. `v2.0-cyanoptera` (`d25d1ce513a`; the code is
the same on `main`) is compared with and without this commit, both built
with the same `make release`. Runs alternate between the two builds, 10
per cell; values are medians.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| A query whose work ends on one slow task, 8 threads: process CPU |
5.99 s | 4.32 s (−28%) |
| The same query: collecting thread CPU | 2.22 s | 0.25 s |
| The same query: wall time | 2.22 s | 2.28 s |
| 48 threads × 48 connections: throughput | 1762 qps | 2027 qps (+15%),
with 14% less CPU |
| Lock-contention futex calls (8 threads × 16 connections) | 17.7k |
0.6k |

**Costs:**
- **Tiny queries:** about 25–40 µs more at p50 (`SELECT 42`: 391 → 416
µs). Work that ends on a worker now pays a condition-variable wake-up
instead of being seen at once by a spinning thread.
- **Large ORDER BY:** a 20M-row ORDER BY at 48 threads is about 10%
slower at the median (0.208 → 0.228 s), while its p95 improved (0.264 →
0.246 s). It goes through many short pipeline phases, so it pays that
wake-up repeatedly.
- **Everything else measured:** wall time is within noise. That covers
GROUP BY, join, serial source, the streaming control and 8-thread
concurrency.

If the tiny-query cost matters, the loop could spin briefly before it
waits. I left that out to keep the change minimal.


Full benchmark tables and method

**Method:**
- A small C++ driver on `Connection::Query` (materialized), with
`Connection::Submit` + `QueryResultStream::Fetch` as a streaming
control.
- In-memory database, GCC 14.2, jemalloc.
- Collecting-thread CPU comes from `/proc/self/task//schedstat`.
- Futex calls were attributed with `perf record -e
syscalls:sys_enter_futex --call-graph dwarf`.

Long materialized queries:

| query | threads | wall | process CPU | collecting thread CPU |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| skewed row groups: `SELECT sum(list_sum(range(i // 100))) FROM t`
(360k rows) | 8 | 2.22 → 2.28 s (p95 2.34 → 2.39) | 5.99 → 4.32 s | 2.22
→ 0.25 s |
| same | 48 | 2.26 → 2.26 s | 6.05 → 4.31 s | 2.26 → 0.53 s |
| `string_agg(… ORDER BY …)`, 2M rows, 4 groups | 8 | 0.161 → 0.152 s |
0.85 → 0.71 s | 0.161 → 0.044 s |
| GROUP BY, 2M groups over 200M rows | 8 / 48 | 1.950 → 1.941 / 0.635 →
0.662 s | flat | flat or lower |
| join + agg over 200M rows | 8 / 48 | 2.571 → 2.567 / 0.517 → 0.488 s |
flat | flat or lower |
| ORDER BY 20M rows | 8 / 48 | 0.789 → 0.795 / 0.208 → 0.228 s (p95
0.264 → 0.246) | flat | lower |
| serial `range()` source, GROUP BY | 8 / 48 | 3.015 → 2.970 / 2.979 →
2.982 s | flat | flat or lower |

Short queries (10k per cell):

| query | threads | p50 | p99 | > 15 ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SELECT 42` | 8 | 391 → 416 µs | 431 → 465 µs | 0 → 0 |
| `SELECT 42` | 48 | 395 → 424 µs | 501 → 543 µs | 0 → 0 |
| `sum` over 10k rows | 8 | 727 → 767 µs | 776 → 814 µs | 0 → 0 |
| `sum` over 10k rows | 48 | 742 → 776 µs | 798 → 871 µs | 0 → 0 |
| filter + agg over 2M rows | 8 | 3661 → 3762 µs | 3905 → 4076 µs | 2 →
0 |
| GROUP BY over 2M rows | 48 | 3972 → 3990 µs | 6014 → 6057 µs | 0 → 0 |

Concurrent connections (300 queries each over 2M rows; 3 runs per cell):

| threads × connections | throughput | process CPU |
|---|---|---|
| 8 × 4, 8 × 16, 8 × 48 | flat (±2%) | flat or slightly lower |
| 48 × 48, filter + agg | 1762 → 2027 qps | 370 → 319 s |
| 48 × 48, GROUP BY | 1021 → 1152 qps | 642 → 570 s |

**Futex breakdown** (8 threads × 16 connections): the total is about the
same (48.5k → 49.8k), but what the calls are changes.
- Before: lock contention from the spin: 8.1k calls in
`GetTaskFromProducer`, 6.1k in `IdleState`, 3.5k in `ScheduleTasks`.
- After: 0.6k calls are contention. The rest are condition-variable
sleeps (13.7k in `WaitForTask`) and wakes (7.8k in `UnregisterTask`).




### Also fixes a DuckDB-Wasm deadlock

With pthreads, a remote `LOAD` sometimes hangs. The steps:
1. `LOAD` runs as a pipeline task. When a scheduler thread picks it up,
the query thread spins in `CompleteInternal`.
2. Emscripten's `dlopen` on the main thread waits in
`_emscripten_proxy_dlsync` until every pthread has synced the new
module.
3. A pthread only syncs while it waits in `emscripten_futex_wait`. The
spinning thread never waits, so the load never finishes.

With this change the collecting thread waits, and the load completes.

### Testing

Release build: `[api]`, `[capi]`, `[capi_v2]`, `[query_result]`,
`[query_result_stream]`, `[stream_buffer]`, `[query_result_arrow]`,
`[appender]` and the interrupt/cancel tests pass. The default `unittest`
run passes except `test/issues/general/test_17757.test`, which fails on
this machine with and without the change.

description:
Report out of memory instead of aborting in worker threads, task errors and stack traces (#27629)

Keeps DuckDB from aborting the process when an allocation fails in
worker thread bookkeeping, in recording a task error, or in resolving a
stack trace.

Combines the PRs labeled `Ready To Merge` in
https://github.com/duckdb-bot/duckdb/pulls below, on top of the current
head of `main`. The changes of each PR are applied as one squashed
commit.

## Changes applied (3 PRs)

- duckdb-bot/duckdb#147: Keep worker threads running when their own
bookkeeping cannot allocate, instead of aborting the process
- duckdb-bot/duckdb#157: Report an out of memory error when a task
cannot record its error, instead of ending the process
- duckdb-bot/duckdb#185: Leave the stack trace unresolved when
backtrace_symbols cannot allocate, instead of crashing

## Original descriptions


duckdb-bot/duckdb#147: Keep worker threads running
when their own bookkeeping cannot allocate, instead of aborting the
process

Near a memory or address space limit, DuckDB could abort the whole
process instead of returning an out of memory error, with `terminate
called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'` or `Fatal glibc
error: failed to register TLS destructor: out of memory`. We found this
while fixing duckdblabs/bot-issue-tracker#174. We measured the CLI on
`main` at `0b272c23b19`, with the source changes of
duckdb-bot/duckdb#122 applied, on a shared 96-core machine loaded by
other test runs. Without those changes, the segmentation fault they fix
happens first. Under a 2 GB address space limit, `SELECT 42` aborted in
14 of 375 runs: 9 on `std::bad_alloc`, 5 on the TLS destructor. Under
300 MB, a large `CREATE TABLE` aborted in 14 of 45 runs: 11 on the TLS
destructor, 3 on `std::bad_alloc`, instead of returning its `Out of
Memory` error. duckdb/duckdb#24965 also reports crashes under memory
pressure.

Worker threads run `TaskScheduler::ExecuteForever` in
`src/parallel/task_scheduler.cpp` without an exception handler, so an
exception escaping it ends the process. The worker's own bookkeeping
allocates: creating its `ConsumerToken`, copying settings into the
`thread_local` cache of `GlobalUserSettings::GetSettings` for idle and
exit flushes and each task's execution mode, calling `Enqueue` for
unfinished tasks, and calling `Executor::AddToBeRescheduled` for blocked
tasks. For a thread that never ran a task, such a settings read also
creates the cache. If glibc cannot allocate its destructor registration,
it aborts without throwing, so no catch can help. The block allocator's
`thread_local` state has the same problem on first use. Catching
exceptions alone is also insufficient: moving on drops the held task and
leaves its query waiting forever.

As requested in review, one try/catch now wraps the whole worker loop of
`ExecuteForever` and catches every exception, including those outside
`std::exception`. `BlockAllocator::ThreadExit` runs after the loop in
its own try/catch, allowing the thread to return its memory even when
its exit flush throws. A `WorkerTask` holds the task and records its
progress. After a catch and a 10 ms wait, the worker continues that task
before taking another: it runs an unstarted task, using the default mode
if reading the mode setting fails, retries enqueuing an unfinished task,
or retries descheduling a blocked task. No task runs twice, and a
stopping worker first finishes the task it holds. If that same task
still fails after 1000 retries, about 10 s, the worker rethrows and ends
the process as on `main`; retrying forever would leave `SET threads` and
shutdown waiting on its join, while dropping the task would leave its
waiter hanging without an error. Exceptions from `Task::Execute` itself
are still rethrown because the task failed to report its own error and
cannot be dropped or rerun. Only threads that ran a task call
`BlockAllocator::ThreadFlush`, which reads settings.
`BlockAllocator::ReturnThreadLocalBlocks`, called by `ThreadFlush`,
`ThreadIdle`, `ThreadExit` and `FlushPool`, clears a thread's block
allocator state only if it already exists, tracked by a plain
`thread_local bool` in `src/storage/block_allocator.cpp`. Threads that
never allocated a block therefore create no block allocator state.
Remaining problems include `PushError(ErrorData(ex))` in
`ExecutorTask::Execute` throwing `std::bad_alloc` and ending the
process, addressed by duckdb-bot/duckdb#157; a wakeup on another thread
spinning in `Executor::RescheduleTask` while the worker retries
descheduling the same task; task destruction with profiling enabled; and
a thread's first task filling the settings cache through its execution
mode read when memory is already gone. That last case includes idle
workers: after the decay delay, every idle worker runs
`BlockAllocator::ThreadIdle`, which can schedule a
`BlockAllocatorFlushTask`. Any worker that never ran a task, including
the one scheduling it, can take it as its first task.
`test/api/test_worker_exception.cpp` makes a blocked task's `Deschedule`
throw and checks that the worker waits at least 10 ms before every
retry, executes the task once, and keeps running tasks; retries
exceptions outside `std::exception`; and deschedules its held task
before stopping. A slow test checks that persistent failure escapes
`ExecuteForever` after exactly 1001 attempts. With the scheduler from
`main` at `9ca79384fa4`, the first and third tests end in `terminate
called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'`, the second in
`terminate called after throwing an instance of 'NonStandardError'`, and
the slow test fails because the exception escapes on the first attempt.
With duckdb-bot/duckdb#122 and this change under the same load, `SELECT
42` under 2 GB aborted in 1 of 375 runs, on `std::bad_alloc`, while
`CREATE TABLE` under 300 MB returned its `Out of Memory` error in all 45
runs. These measurements preceded the retry cap, but every run took well
under a second, far below the cap's roughly 10 s. On an older `main`,
all 6 aborts traced in 992 runs with this change came from error
reporting in `ExecutorTask::Execute`. The shell test covering these
cases was removed in review: without duckdb-bot/duckdb#122 every run
segfaults and the test only skips; with it, the test can still fail
until duckdb-bot/duckdb#157 is merged. All unit tests pass on `reldebug`
except `test/sql/settings/reset/reset_threads.test`, which also fails on
`main` on this machine. Benchmarks from an earlier round against `main`
at `0af6d8fc3ab`, using 16 threads, were within noise: TPC-H SF1 `q01`
+0.3%, `q09` -0.6%, `q18` +0.1%, `create_art` +0.1%, and `simple_group`
+0.4%.

Fixes duckdblabs/bot-issue-tracker#578





duckdb-bot/duckdb#157: Report an out of memory error
when a task cannot record its error, instead of ending the
process

Near a memory or address space limit, a worker could abort the process
with `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'`
instead of failing the query with an out of memory error. During review
of duckdb-bot/duckdb#147, with duckdb-bot/duckdb#122 and
duckdb-bot/duckdb#147 applied, CLI runs of `SELECT 42` under a 2 GB
address space limit aborted in 6 of 992 runs on 96 cores, all while
reporting a task's error. We could not reproduce another abort here:
about 5500 runs of that reproducer and a large `CREATE TABLE` under 300
MB, at address space limits from 1.6 to 2.6 GB, succeeded or returned an
`Out of Memory Error`.

`ExecutorTask::Execute` (`src/parallel/executor_task.cpp`), and
`TaskExecutorTask::Execute` and `RunGuarded`
(`src/parallel/task_executor.cpp`), catch task exceptions and call
`PushError(ErrorData(ex))`. Creating `ErrorData` and appending it to the
errors of `TaskErrorManager` allocate; parsing a JSON message can also
throw another exception when memory runs out. That exception escapes
`Task::Execute` and the worker loop, ending the process. Reporting the
error also interrupts other pipelines, which reschedules blocked tasks
and can fail the same way.

`TaskErrorManager::PushTaskError`
(`src/include/duckdb/execution/task_error_manager.hpp`) takes a callable
that creates the error. If creating or recording the first error fails
with `std::bad_alloc`, it records that loss without allocating;
`GetError` and `ThrowException` then report `Failed to allocate memory
to report the error of a task`, an out of memory error allocated once
when the first error manager is created. Any other exception propagates
as before. Since `ErrorData` parses the JSON message of an exception,
`JSONDocument::TryParse` and `JSONValue::ToString`
(`src/common/json_document.cpp`) now throw `std::bad_alloc` when yyjson
fails to allocate, instead of a parse or serialization error. Later
errors that cannot be recorded are dropped because only the first error
is reported. All six catch blocks use this through new `PushTaskError`
overloads of `Executor` and `TaskExecutor`. From a task, the executor
interrupts other pipelines on a best effort basis, setting the interrupt
state first; if rescheduling a blocked task fails, the main thread still
sees the recorded error through its timed wait and cancels remaining
tasks. `StateWithBlockableTasks::UnblockTasks` takes blocked tasks
before invoking callbacks, so a throwing callback leaves none to be
called twice, which would spin in `Executor::RescheduleTask`. Other
worker allocations remain outside scope, including those listed in the
related worker bookkeeping PR duckdb-bot/duckdb#147.
`test/api/test_task_error_out_of_memory.cpp` makes the callable throw
`std::bad_alloc`, checking that the out of memory error is reported,
stays first and is cleared by `Reset`; it also checks that a
`SerializationException` from the callable escapes and records nothing,
and that `TryParse` throws `std::bad_alloc` for a length yyjson reports
as an allocation failure. No unit test forces real allocations to fail.
A probe that fails the k-th allocation of 1 MB or more while
`PushTaskError` records a `std::runtime_error` with a 4 MB JSON message
recorded the out of memory error for every k, while with only the
narrowed catch the failures inside yyjson escaped as
`SerializationException`. The reproducer did not fail on the base here,
so duckdblabs/bot-issue-tracker#594 is related rather than fixed. All
unit tests pass on reldebug except failures also present on `main` here.
On relassert with sanitizers, the new tests, the API, scheduler, error,
Arrow, Parquet JSON and geometry tests pass, as do the parallelism tests
except `concurrent_writes_during_index_creation`, which also fails on
`main`. Benchmarks against `main`, with 8 threads and machine load of 70
to 90, put TPC-H SF1 q01, q09 and q18, `simple_group`, `create_art`,
`partitioned_scan` and `row_number` within 3%;
`to_parquet_partition_by_few` measured -3.5%, and
`to_parquet_partition_by_many` +5.4% and +4.4% in two runs, while an A/A
run of `main` against itself moved +5.2% in its first samples. The copy
operator does not call the changed `UnblockTasks`. Also related are
duckdb-bot/duckdb#122, the jemalloc segmentation fault encountered first
on `main`, and duckdb/duckdb#24965, a separate related report of crashes
under memory pressure.

Related: duckdblabs/bot-issue-tracker#594





duckdb-bot/duckdb#185: Leave the stack trace
unresolved when backtrace_symbols cannot allocate, instead of
crashing

DuckDB could end with a segmentation fault instead of reporting an error
if memory ran out while building an INTERNAL exception’s message. Every
INTERNAL error resolves its stack trace during message construction, in
task catch blocks (`ExecutorTask::Execute`, `TaskExecutor`) and when the
client context finalizes an error. This surfaced while answering a
review of duckdb-bot/duckdb#157; v1.5.6 contains the same code.

In `src/common/stacktrace.cpp`, `StackTrace::ResolveStacktraceSymbols`
passed the result of `backtrace_symbols` to the loop that formats each
frame without checking it. When `backtrace_symbols` could not allocate
memory, it returned NULL, and the loop read through a null pointer.

The change leaves the stack trace unresolved and returns an empty string
when `backtrace_symbols` returns NULL, matching platforms without stack
traces. The error keeps its type and message, without resolved frames;
throwing `std::bad_alloc` could interrupt building or delivering the
original error. There is no repository test: `backtrace_symbols` only
fails through `malloc`, and DuckDB has no allocator failure hook for it.
The issue’s program replaces `malloc` and `realloc` to fail the k-th
allocation while building `ErrorData` from an `InternalException`. On
main, k=27 ends in a segmentation fault; with the change, no k from 1 to
80 crashes, and k=27 builds the INTERNAL error. All unit tests pass on
reldebug except failures that `main` has on this machine too. Error
tests pass on a relassert build with sanitizers. There is no benchmark
because the change adds one check on the error path. The related
duckdblabs/bot-issue-tracker#594 and duckdb-bot/duckdb#157 make task
error reporting survive allocation failures using catch blocks, which
cannot help here because a segmentation fault cannot be caught.

description:
Handle infinite timestamps in date arithmetic, cast statistics, avg and far-apart subtraction (#27627)

Fixes wrong results and errors for infinite and extreme timestamps:
monotone and cast statistics dropping infinities, date arithmetic with
-infinity, avg over values that include infinity, and subtracting
timestamps far apart.

Combines the PRs labeled `Ready To Merge` in
https://github.com/duckdb-bot/duckdb/pulls below, on top of the current
head of `main`. The changes of each PR are applied as one squashed
commit.

## Changes applied (4 PRs)

- duckdb-bot/duckdb#168: Handle `-infinity` correctly in date arithmetic
and monotone statistics
- duckdb-bot/duckdb#169: Cast statistics include the casts of the
infinities between the bounds
- duckdb-bot/duckdb#156: Return the infinity as the average of
timestamps that include one, and NULL when they include both
- duckdb-bot/duckdb#189: Subtract timestamps far apart without
overflowing when the result fits

## Original descriptions


duckdb-bot/duckdb#168: Handle `-infinity` correctly in
date arithmetic and monotone statistics

On a DATE column containing `make_date(-2147483647 - 1)`, `-infinity`
and `1970-01-01`, `count(last_day(c))` returned 3 although
`last_day('-infinity')` is NULL. The same miscount affected `epoch_ns`
on TIMESTAMP_NS and TIMESTAMPTZ_NS, `date_diff`, `date_sub`, and ICU
`era`, `isoyear`, `date_diff` and `date_sub`. `WHERE c + 2 =
'-infinity'::DATE` dropped a matching row, while `make_date(i) + 2`
could fail with `INTERNAL Error: Monotonic arg annotation violated for
"+"`. ICU `date_trunc('era', x)` hit the same internal error across the
BC/AD boundary.

Without a custom statistics callback,
`StatisticsPropagator::PropagateMonotoneBounds` evaluates the function
at the bounds of its arguments. The smallest finite DATE or TIMESTAMP
sorts below `-infinity`, so finite bounds can contain it. DATE plus or
minus INTEGER preserved `-infinity` but moved the date below it past it;
ICU era truncation moved BC timestamps into AD and back. Neither was
monotone. The other functions are monotone on finite values but return
NULL for `-infinity`, which evaluation at the bounds misses unless it is
a bound.

DATE plus or minus INTEGER now rejects inputs and results below
`-infinity` with `Date out of range`, and ICU era truncation loses its
monotone annotation. Functions returning NULL for infinite arguments use
`StatisticsPropagator::PropagateFiniteMonotoneBounds`, which gives no
bounds when an argument range contains `-infinity` and otherwise uses
`PropagateMonotoneBounds`, unchanged from main.
`test/optimizer/statistics/statistics_monotone_infinity.test` covers
each function, both argument positions and date arithmetic errors; it
fails on main and passes with this change.
`test/optimizer/statistics/monotonicity_annotations.test` covers ICU era
truncation. `test/sql/optimizer/monotone_function_zonemap_pruning.test`
confirms that `date_diff` and `epoch_ns` still prune through the
callback, scanning the same number of row groups as main. Tests in the
touched area pass under reldebug and relassert with sanitizers. The full
reldebug suite fails only `test/sql/settings/reset/reset_threads.test`,
which also fails on main under the machine's thread limit. The preimage
rewrite (duckdblabs/bot-issue-tracker#609), date part statistics
callbacks (duckdb-bot/duckdb#166) and cast statistics
(duckdblabs/bot-issue-tracker#607) remain separate problems.

Fixes duckdblabs/bot-issue-tracker#608





duckdb-bot/duckdb#169: Cast statistics include the
casts of the infinities between the bounds

Filtering a `TIMESTAMP_NS` column cast to `TIMESTAMP`, `TIMESTAMP_MS` or
`DATE` dropped `-infinity` rows when the column also contained its
smallest finite value. An equality filter returned 0 instead of 1, while
`count(*) FILTER (...)` found the row. Ranges ending at `-infinity` also
lost finite matches, and `TIMESTAMPTZ_NS` casts to `TIMESTAMPTZ` had the
same problem.

`CastStatistics::TryPropagate` computed cast statistics using only the
minimum and maximum. The smallest finite date or timestamp sorts below
the `-infinity` sentinel, but its cast can sort above it. This left the
cast of `-infinity` outside the computed bounds, so the optimizer pruned
matching rows.

We now order the cast bounds for date and timestamp sources and widen
them to include casts of infinities within the original bounds.
`test/optimizer/statistics/statistics_cast_infinity.test` covers
infinity equality, ranges and the affected casts; it fails on main and
passes with the change. A probe across all date and timestamp cast
combinations found three count mismatches on main and none after the
fix. The optimizer, timestamp and date type and function, and cast
suites pass on reldebug and on relassert with sanitizers. The full unit
suite passes except for one test that also fails on main in the same
configuration.

Fixes duckdblabs/bot-issue-tracker#607





duckdb-bot/duckdb#156: Return the infinity as the
average of timestamps that include one, and NULL when they include
both

`avg` over TIMESTAMP, TIMESTAMPTZ and DATE values containing infinity
returned finite timestamps. Averaging `-infinity` with `2000-01-01`
returned `144155-06-27 (BC) 21:59:32.612097`; `infinity` with
`2000-01-01` returned `148123-07-07 02:00:27.387903`; and `infinity`
with `-infinity` returned `1970-01-01 00:00:00`. With the smallest
timestamp, `290309-12-22 (BC) 00:00:00`, the average fell below the
timestamp range, and casting it to VARCHAR failed with an INTERNAL
error. v1.5.6 returns the same values.

`DiscreteAverageOperation` in
`extension/core_functions/aggregate/algebraic/avg.cpp` sums timestamp
microsecond counts in an `AvgState` and divides by the count.
The infinities are sentinels, INT64_MAX and -INT64_MAX, but were
included in the sum as ordinary microsecond counts.

The new `TimestampAverageOperation` returns the infinity present, or
NULL when both signs occur, where `avg` over DOUBLE returns NaN. NULL
avoids an error in SUMMARIZE, which averages every timestamp column. It
keeps the 24 byte state of `main`: after seeing an infinity, no sum is
needed, so count is set to `NumericLimits::Maximum()`
(18446744073709551615) and value records 1 for `infinity`, 2 for
`-infinity`, or 3 for both. Each finite value costs one comparison of
the count and is skipped once the count is the maximum. Combining finite
states fails if their count overflows or reaches the maximum; a state
with count 0 is empty whatever its value. A separate state with two
counters (40 bytes) or two flags (32 bytes) made the grouped benchmark
21% and 11% slower, respectively, because the hash table is bound by
state size. Exported states (`EXPORT_STATE`) retain `{count, value}`; an
infinity state exports as `{'count': 18446744073709551615, 'value': 1}`.
Importing a state with that count and a value other than 1, 2 or 3 fails
with an error. Builds of `main` before this change read such a state as
a timestamp just before `1970-01-01`. No release uses this layout;
releases export states as BLOB.
`test/sql/aggregate/aggregates/test_avg_timestamp_infinity.test` fails
on `main` and covers both signs, both infinities, SUMMARIZE, DATE,
TIMESTAMPTZ, the smallest timestamp, constants, DISTINCT and ordered
aggregates, 400000 rows scanned by 4 threads and window frames.
`test/sql/aggregate/aggregate_state_export/avg_timestamp_export_state.test`
covers exported, combined, repeated, imported and rejected states. All
unit tests pass on reldebug except failures also present on `main` on
this machine; aggregate tests also pass with
`debug_verify_aggregate_state_export` except five failures also present
on `main`. Aggregate, window and timestamp tests pass on a relassert
build with sanitizers. Two new benchmarks in `benchmark/micro/aggregate`
are listed in `.github/regression/micro.csv`. Against `main`,
`simple_aggregate`, `simple_group`, `avg_with_stddev` and TPC-H SF1 q01
are within 3%. With 8 threads, `avg_timestamp` went from 4.3 ms to 2.2
ms and `avg_timestamp_grouped` from 22.3 ms to 22.4 ms; with 1 thread,
from 28.5 ms to 13.6 ms and from 89.0 ms to 92.5 ms (medians of 30
runs). We did not look into why `avg_timestamp` got faster. This was
found while reviewing duckdb-bot/duckdb#25; another pull request fixes
`median` and `quantile_cont` over infinite timestamps, tracked in
duckdblabs/bot-issue-tracker#591.

Fixes duckdblabs/bot-issue-tracker#590





duckdb-bot/duckdb#189: Subtract timestamps far apart
without overflowing when the result fits

Subtracting timestamps more than about 292277 years apart failed even
when the result fit. For example, `SELECT TIMESTAMP '294247-01-10' -
TIMESTAMP '290309-12-22 (BC)'` raised `Conversion Error: Timestamp
difference is out of bounds` instead of returning `213503982 days`.
Similarly, `date_sub('hour', TIMESTAMP '290309-12-22 (BC)', TIMESTAMP
'2000-01-01')` raised `Out of Range Error: Overflow in subtraction of
INT64` instead of returning `2562310752`, although `date_diff('hour',
...)` already returned that count. This also affected `date_sub` with
millisecond to week units and ICU's `date_sub` and `date_diff` on
`TIMESTAMPTZ` with millisecond to minute units. DuckDB 1.5.6 behaves the
same way. We found this while answering a review on
duckdb-bot/duckdb#25; there is no duckdb/duckdb issue.

The problem is that `Interval::GetDifference` in
`src/common/types/interval.cpp`, `DateSub::SubtractMicros` in
core_functions' `date_sub.cpp`, and
`ICUCalendarSub::SubtractMicrosecond` in `icu-datesub.cpp` subtract the
microsecond counts in an `int64` before converting the difference to
days or units. Finite timestamps span about 584554 years, but an `int64`
can only hold about 292277 years in microseconds. The intermediate
subtraction can therefore overflow even when the requested result fits.
The `date_sub` overflow check came from duckdb/duckdb#4985, which
replaced undefined behavior with this error.

The change keeps the `int64` subtraction as the fast path and falls back
to `HUGEINT` on overflow. `GetDifference` splits that difference into
days and microseconds; the days between two finite timestamps always
fit. A new `Interval::GetDifferenceInUnits` divides by a unit and raises
an out of range error if the count still does not fit. Microsecond units
retain their overflow error because the result does not fit a `BIGINT`.
`date_sub` and ICU keep inline `int64` paths with compile time constant
units: calling the helper per row with a runtime divisor initially made
`date_sub('hour')` about 17 percent slower over 50M rows. With the
constant, it measures 0.080 s against 0.078 s on main, within the noise
also seen for unchanged TIMESTAMP subtraction (0.103 s against 0.101 s),
using a hot CLI with one untimed and five timed runs.
`test/sql/function/timestamp/test_timestamp_difference_range.test`
covers subtraction at both ends of the range in both directions, sub-day
remainders, every `date_sub` unit against a `HUGEINT` calculation,
microsecond overflow, and ICU `date_sub` and `date_diff` with fractional
endpoints; it fails on main and passes with the change.
`date_sub.test_slow` and
`test/fuzzer/sqlsmith/timestamp_diff_overflow.test` now check values
where they previously expected overflow errors for results that fit.
Timestamp, date and interval function and type tests, plus sqlsmith
fuzzer tests, pass in both a release build with debug info and a build
with sanitizers and assertions. All unit tests pass in the former and
all non-slow unit tests in the latter, except
`test/sql/settings/reset/reset_threads.test`: it fails in both suites
and on main because they ran with `unittest --max-threads`, and passes
without that option.

Fixes duckdblabs/bot-issue-tracker#629

test: mock the extensions API in integration tests (#8640)

Some of the CLI's tests were quietly calling Netlify's real extensions
service when they should only talk to the fake API server they run
against. A recent change started sending the tests' fake login token
with that call. The real service rejects that token, and the CLI then
carried on without any site information, which broke a test that checks
the account ID. This sends that call to the fake server during tests and
turns the check back on. Nothing changes for people using the CLI.

## What changed

- `BaseCommand.getConfig` now passes `testOpts` to `resolveConfig` when
`NETLIFY_API_URL` points at a loopback host (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`,
`[::1]`). This goes through a new `getLocalApiTestOpts` helper in
`src/utils/local-api-test-opts.ts`. In `@netlify/config`,
`testOpts.host` only decides where the extensions request goes; the API
client already gets the same host. `netlify build` (`src/lib/build.ts`)
already passes `testOpts` for any `NETLIFY_API_URL`. This path is
limited to loopback hosts because `@netlify/config` sends the request,
token included, over plain `http://` to any host that isn't a Netlify
one.
- The mock extensions routes in `tests/integration/utils/mock-api.ts`
now match any site or account ID; before, they matched only the literal
`site_id` / `account_id`. The same routes are added to
`tests/integration/utils/mock-api-vitest.ts`, which had none.
- The `account.id` assertion in
`tests/integration/commands/dev/v2-api.test.ts`, commented out in #8639,
is back.

Background: netlify/build#7268 removed the
`send_build_bot_token_to_jigsaw` flag, so `@netlify/config` 25.3.0
always sends the token. The real team endpoint returns 403 for
`fake-token`, and `getConfig` then quietly re-resolves offline. Real
users are unaffected: real sites already return
`send_build_bot_token_to_jigsaw: true` to the CLI.

## How it was verified

- `typecheck`, `lint`, `format:check` and `test:unit` all pass (756
tests).
- `v2-api.test.ts` passes, 24 of 24. With the old `base-command.ts`,
"receives context" fails with the same `account.id` error CI showed.
- `dev.test.ts`, `build-program.test.ts`, `build.test.ts` and
`telemetry.test.ts` pass.
- **Draft because:** the Codex review passes (simplicity, security,
spec) haven't run. Every attempt was rate-limited with a 429. The full
CI suite is the other remaining check.

Closes EX-3522

Supabase CLI v2.122.0 — 2026-10-23

This release is mostly fixes. The headline changes are supabase/supabase.lock for pinning stack service versions, PGSSL* and TLS settings now reaching db push --linked and pg_dump, and clearer config parse errors. Several fixes cover start/stop on Podman and stack reliability.

Highlights

  • Pin stack service versions in a lock file — stack mode can run any published service version, match your hosted project after supabase link, and reproduce the whole local stack from a committed supabase/supabase.lock. (#7195)
  • Postgres TLS settings now apply to db push --linked and pg_dump — PGSSLMODE, PGSSLROOTCERT, and PGSSLCERT/PGSSLKEY are read from your shell on direct connections, and remote db dump and the first db pull pass the resolved TLS settings through. Before, verify-full was ignored and client-cert servers rejected the dump. (#7261, #7266)

New features

  • supabase --help shows token permissions — every command's help now has a PERMISSIONS section listing the personal access token permissions it needs, so you can scope tokens for CI without guessing. (#7268)
  • supabase stack can run any published service version — the lock file (see Highlights) also lets you try a hotfix or match production versions. (#7195)

Improvements

  • Config errors say what's wrong and where — start, status, stop, and functions serve used to print a bare CliConfigParseError. They now point to the bad line. inf and nan numbers are rejected at load time instead of slipping through. (#7267)
  • Heads-up: the default target is changing — the CLI now warns before the upcoming switch to a local default target. Check your scripts if you rely on the current default. (#7186)
  • db pull and pg_dump honor TLS config — see Highlights. (#7266)

Bug fixes

  • supabase start and stop no longer fail every few runs on Podman — when there's no docker on PATH (macOS with podman machine), you no longer hit failed to inspect docker image or ssh: handshake failed: EOF. (#7270)
  • supabase stop --no-backup no longer exits 1 with older Docker CLIs — it works with Docker CLI older than 23.0 talking to a newer daemon. (#7177)
  • Piping CLI output into head or another reader that exits early exits cleanly — the CLI used to crash with Unknown: Stdio.stdout (exit 1), and with --output json it could hang forever. It now exits 0. (#7175)
  • db diff --from linked --to linked no longer fails without a database password — it used to fail with password authentication failed for user "cli_login_postgres" when no password was set via --password, SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD, or supabase/.env. (#7139)
  • functions deploy --use-api uploads multiline dynamic imports — functions with import( split across lines, or with import attributes, no longer throw Module not found after deploy. (#7282)
  • supabase init test OTP example works — the [auth.sms.test_otp] example now includes the country code, so +14152127777 gets the test code instead of sending a real SMS. (#7279)
  • Stack: concurrent native stacks no longer share a backend port — two stacks started at once could bind Logflare to the same private port. (#7184)
  • Stack: idle gateway connections stay open for 75 s — a short pause between API calls no longer ends in TypeError: fetch failed. (#7193)
  • Stack: local Studio logs work again — analytics is pinned to Logflare 1.50.15, so logs pages no longer show "Backend error". (#7182)
  • Stack: rest starts when a db_pre_request hook rejects requests without an app header — it used to hang on readiness. (#7216)
  • Stack: native launches are more reliable — the launcher waits for a cache lock instead of failing, and Realtime waits for its own bind line before it's marked ready. (#7145)

feat(cli): carry plan-gate entitlement on machine-mode errors (#7271)

Plan-gated Management API denials already return `{ error: { code:
"entitlement_required", feature, upgrade_url } }`. In `--output-format
json` and `stream-json` that signal only survives as escaped text inside
`error.message`, so an agent has to parse prose to learn that an upgrade
is needed and where. I added a structured `entitlement` to the
machine-mode error object for every command whose status errors go
through `mapHttpError`.

```json
{"_tag":"Error","error":{"code":"DomainsUnexpectedStatusError","message":"...","entitlement":{"feature":"custom_domain","upgrade_url":"https://supabase.com/dashboard/org//billing"}}}
```

**Changed:**
- **Machine-mode errors carry the plan gate**: on a 4xx, `mapHttpError`
decodes the untruncated body and, when it is the plan-gate envelope,
attaches `entitlement: { feature, upgrade_url }` to the status error.
`normalizeCliError` passes it into the json and stream-json error
object, so commands with no per-command upgrade wiring (`branches
unpause`) get it too.
- **Handlers that rebuild a mapped error keep it**: `branches
create`/`update`, `vanity-subdomains activate`/`check-availability` and
`sso list`/`add`/`update`/`remove` forward the field, and `Output.fail`
declares it in its type.
- **Envelope values are validated in one place**: I moved the parser
into `http-errors.ts` and `suggestUpgrade` reuses it. `feature` must be
a plain key and `upgrade_url` an http(s) URL without credentials,
emitted as the parsed URL so control and bidi characters arrive
percent-encoded; anything else counts as no envelope.

**Note:** text output and `cli_upgrade_suggested` are unchanged for
well-formed envelopes. The per-command text hint stays until I move the
hint and the event onto the same central path in a follow-up.

description:
ci: bump toolchains and upgrade mise-action to v5 (#7285)

## Toolchain bumps

- Bumps pnpm, node, bun, and mise. `mise.lock` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` are
updated to match.
- Updates the mise version pinned in each GitHub Actions workflow.
- Drops `pnpm exec` from `bun` commands. The toolchain setup already
puts bun on `PATH`, so running it through pnpm only added a process hop
and a pnpm lookup. Calling bun directly removes that overhead and
complexity.

## Workflow changes

### flaky-check installs bun with `oven-sh/setup-bun`

Its plan and report jobs only need bun. setup-bun restores a 34 MB cache
with just the bun binary. mise-action restored a 68 MB mise data
directory and then ran a locked install and a listing on top, which took
about twice as long on a cache hit. Every other bun-only step in the
repository already uses setup-bun, so this makes them consistent.

### `jdx/mise-action` moves from v4.3.0 to v5.2.2

What we gain:

- **The mise binary is verified before it runs.** A downloaded binary is
checked against the release's signed manifest, and a binary restored
from cache is checked against the signed release checksums. Before, a
cached binary could run unchecked.
- **The job's GitHub token stays inside the action.** v4 wrote it to the
environment of every later step. Now only the action sees it.
- **Caches rebuild every 30 days.** GitHub never evicts a cache that
keeps getting hits, so a busy repository could keep the same tools for
months. The default key now rolls over on a schedule.

What does not change for us: every step pins a mise version, so the new
release-age default does not apply, and the pinned mise ships the signed
manifest the action now requires.

One thing to expect: the default cache key format changed, so each mise
cache misses once after this lands. The sync check job runs `mise
install` in a later step. It no longer gets the token, but it fetches
release metadata through mise's own relay and downloads assets directly
from GitHub releases, so it never used the token.

### The shared setup action drops its custom `cache_key`

The custom key hashed `mise.toml`, `mise.lock`, `.node-version`,
`.bun-version`, and `package.json`. mise-action's default key already
covers `mise.toml` and `mise.lock`, plus the requested tool subset, the
runner image, and the mise version. The lockfile pins the node, bun, and
pnpm versions the version files select, and a locked install refuses any
version the lockfile does not have. So the extra hashes could not catch
anything the lockfile hash misses, and the default key is strictly
better.

feat(cli): honor tls settings in `pg_dump` (CLI-2753) (#7266)

## TL;DR

remote `db dump` and the first `db pull` seed now pass the resolved TLS
settings to `pg_dump`
## whats introduced?

`pg_dump` only got host, port, user, password and database, so a
container dump ignored `PGSSLMODE=verify-full`, trusted any CA, and got
turned away by servers that require a client cert.

for the linked project and a remote `--db-url`, it now gets the resolved
`sslmode` and connect timeout, the root cert under `require` or
`verify-*`, and the client cert unless the key needs `sslpassword`
In a container the cert files are mounted read only, and a missing one
fails before docker runs

> [!NOTE]
> a remote dump that only worked because verification was skipped now
fails. local targets and runs without TLS or timeout settings are
unchanged

  remote -- no --> plain["host, port, user, password, database"]

Shutdown gave up on tool bodies after the 5 s listener budget, so a call
blocked inside an RPC method (eth_call ignores the MCP shutdown token and
stops only at JsonRpc.Timeout) could keep reading databases the node was
already disposing. The drain now waits up to max(JsonRpc.Timeout,

stop budget, and logs an error if bodies still outlive it.

orientation; the per-tool detail already lives in nethermind://guide.

* fix(mcp): offer tracing only when the node exposes a replay module

trace_transaction and the explain_transaction call trace now require
debug or trace in JsonRpc.EnabledModules as well as Mcp.EnableTracing,
so MCP does not expose transaction replay on a node whose operator has
switched both replay modules off. trace is in the default module list.

Replaces simple production LINQ with loops per the coding style, and
documents shared RPC resources and the shutdown wait in the README.

* fix(mcp): log client protocol errors at debug level

Reading an unknown resource or prompt made the SDK log an unhandled
handler exception at error level, although the client already gets the
JSON-RPC error. Seen on a mainnet node as an ERROR line for a client
that read nethermind://node/status. Protocol errors caused by the client

Run ruff via uv tool run so the SDK bumper can format pydabs (#7156)

## Changes

- Call ruff as `uv tool run ruff@0.15.17` instead of `uvx ruff@0.15.17`
in `python/Taskfile.yml` (`pydabs-codegen`, `pydabs-fmt`) and the root
`RUFF` var. `uvx` is only an alias for `uv tool run`, so behavior is
unchanged where both exist.
- `bump-sdk` skill: note that the SDK bumper does not log
`bump-sdk-post`'s output and cannot run `test-update` (no `ruff` on its
`PATH`), and correct the claim that `pypi.org` is CI's default index
(CI's test jobs point `UV_INDEX_URL` at a JFrog mirror).

## Why

The SDK bumper's image ships only the `uv` binary, not `uvx`. In the
v0.190.0 bump (#7155), `pydabs-codegen` ran codegen and then failed on
`uvx ruff ... format` (the `ruff check --fix` before it is `|| true`).
The PR therefore carried raw, unformatted pydabs output with circular
imports. That failed `validate-generated`, the Python tests and docs,
and every acceptance test that imports the pydabs wheel. `bump-sdk-post`
stopped at that step, so `test-update` never ran, and
`generate-clijson-post` ignores the error, so nothing surfaced in the
bumper.

The lock-file half of that failure (proxy URLs left in
`python/codegen/uv.lock`) was fixed separately by #6987 (`uv run
--frozen`); this branch has `main` merged with that change.

## Tests

- Reproduced the bumper's failure locally with a `PATH` that has `uv`
but no `uvx`: `pydabs-codegen` on #7155's base produced output
byte-identical to the bumper's commit. With this change and the same
`PATH`, it succeeds, and the pydabs diff shrinks from 703 files to the
13 real SDK changes, all ruff-formatted.
- After merging `main` (with #6987), `pydabs-codegen` without `uvx`
reproduces `main`'s pydabs output exactly and leaves both lock files
untouched.
- `./task lint-python fmt-python checks`.

`acceptance/cmd/aitools/list/`:
- `explicit-ref`: `DATABRICKS_SKILLS_REF` is set. The CLI fetches only
the skills manifest.
- `pinned`: the compat entry pins `0.2.32`. The CLI does not call the
latest-release API.
- `latest`: the compat entry is `latest`, and the API returns `v0.2.33`.
The CLI lists the skills from that release.
- `latest-lookup-fails`: the compat entry is `latest`, and the API
returns 403. The command fails with `resolve latest skills release: HTTP
403 fetching latest skills release`.
- The skills latest-release lookup now reads
`DATABRICKS_CLI_GITHUB_API_URL`, the existing override from
`libs/versioncheck`. `versioncheck.GitHubAPIURL` is now exported, and
both lookups use it. `versioncheck` already owns this variable, so the
helper stays there. The helper now also removes a trailing `/`.
- The `-run` pattern of `test-exp-aitools` now uses top-level
alternation and includes `cmd/aitools`.

`go test` does not split on a `/` inside parentheses. So a change in

acceptance tests also run in this target now. The `sources` do not
change: a change in `acceptance/cmd/aitools` still runs `task test`,
which includes Windows.

No acceptance test ran `aitools list`. The aitools acceptance tests set
`DATABRICKS_SKILLS_REF`, so they never used the compat manifest or the
latest-release lookup. Because of this, the CLI tests did not find the
1.22.0 regression from #7069. The VS Code unit tests found it in
databricks/databricks-vscode#2269, and #7159 mitigates it.

The `latest-lookup-fails` output records the current behavior. When
`aitools list` gets an embedded fallback, the test must change, and the
diff shows the new behavior.

Each test copies a committed `compat-manifest.json` into
`DATABRICKS_CACHE_DIR`. So the result does not depend on the embedded or
the remote compat manifest. `test.toml` also sets
`DATABRICKS_SKILLS_REF`, `DATABRICKS_FORCE_EMBEDDED_COMPAT`, and
`DATABRICKS_CACHE_ENABLED`, so values from the shell do not change the
result.

- `go test ./acceptance -run

all pass, also with `DATABRICKS_SKILLS_REF=main` and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`

(default, override, and trailing `/`).

- The JSON output keeps only `release`, `skills`, and `summary`, because
agent detection depends on the binaries on `PATH`.

`libs/aitools` or `cmd/aitools` runs the new tests on Linux and macOS
only.

PyDABs: Pass --frozen to uv run so the Taskfile never rewrites uv.lock (#6987)

## Changes

The PyDABs `uv run` invocations in `python/Taskfile.yml` now pass
`--frozen`, so
uv consumes the committed `uv.lock` as-is instead of re-resolving. A
plain
`uv run` rewrites the lockfile's registry/package URLs to the internal
`*.databricks.com` PyPI proxy whenever uv/pip is proxy-configured
(locally, or
via setup-jfrog in CI), which surfaces as spurious `uv.lock` /
`codegen/uv.lock`
diffs.

`pydabs-codegen` previously papered over this by reverting the lockfiles
after
generating (`git checkout -- uv.lock codegen/uv.lock`); with `--frozen`
the churn
never happens, so that cleanup is dropped.

`--frozen` is applied to the five project `uv run` calls: `pydabs-test`,
`pydabs-lint` (pyright), `pydabs-docs`, and both `pydabs-codegen` calls.
It is
deliberately *not* added to `uv lock --check` (whose job is to detect a
stale
lock) or to the `--no-project` / lockless `--script` invocations
elsewhere (no
lock to freeze). It matches the existing pattern for
`internal/genkit/tagging.py`,
which already runs `uv run --frozen --script`.

## Why

Running any PyDABs task in a proxy-configured shell left `uv.lock` and
`codegen/uv.lock` dirty with proxy URLs — environment noise that could
be
committed by accident. `--frozen` fixes it at the source rather than
reverting
after the fact.

## Tests

Ran `pydabs-codegen`, `pydabs-docs`, and `pydabs-test` in a
proxy-configured
shell: all pass and leave the working tree clean (no lockfile churn),
with no
change to generated output. `uv run --frozen pyright` runs clean too.
`pydabs-lint` as a whole still stops at its pre-existing `uv lock
--check` step,
which fails on the proxy↔pypi.org URL mismatch — unrelated to this
change.

### CLI

ssh: create the release folder before uploading the tunnel binaries (#7141)

## Changes
`ssh connect` now creates each release folder
(`/databricks_cli__linux_/`) with `mkdirs`
before uploading the archive to `import-file`. `mkdirs` succeeds when
the folder already exists. `CreateParentDirectories` stays as the
fallback if the upload still gets a 404.

## Why
`import-file` reports a missing parent folder with a 404 only after the
whole archive has been sent. On the first upload of every new version,
the filer then created the folder and sent the archive again. Every
archive (~17 MB) was therefore uploaded twice, and half of the
`import-file` calls showed up as failures.

The upload stays on `import-file`. Moving it to `/workspace/import` was
considered, but `format=AUTO` imports a zip as a new folder that can't
be overwritten. Overwriting is needed for dev builds and for concurrent
connects. It also places an archive with a single top-level file next to
that folder instead of inside it.

## Tests
- `ssh/connect-serverless-feature-disabled` now records the
`import-file` requests: one per architecture. Without the change it
records four.
- New `TestUploadReleasesSendsEachArchiveOnce`: a fresh release upload,
and a dev re-upload into existing folders, both send one `import-file`
request per architecture. Without the change the fresh upload records
the reported pattern: `amd64 404`, `amd64 200`, `arm64 404`, `arm64
200`.
- Against a real AWS workspace with the v1.21.0 release archives: the
old upload made `import-file 404 → mkdirs 200 → import-file 200`. The
new one makes `mkdirs 200 → import-file 200` per architecture, with the
same extracted layout.
- `./task lint-go` and the ssh unit tests pass locally.

This pull request and its description were written by Isaac.

Add opt-in strict profile matching for bundle targets (#7109)

## Changes

Add `DATABRICKS_BUNDLE_STRICT_PROFILE_MATCH`, read as a boolean. When it
is true and the target has a host or workspace ID, a strict loader runs
before the config file, so the profile name always comes from the config
file, even if `DATABRICKS_TOKEN` is set. The host and workspace ID must
match exactly one workspace profile, and a profile without
`workspace_id` only matches targets without one. A target with a
workspace ID but no host must name a profile with that ID. A target with
neither resolves as without strict mode.

The loader does the same lookup as `ResolveProfileFromHost`, but fails
when there is no single match, a different profile is selected, or the
file is missing.

## Why

With env auth the CLI skips host-based profile matching, so the token
goes to whatever host the target sets. A caller that passes its own
token and a file of trusted profiles needs the target checked against
them first, including on a custom host shared by several workspaces.

## Tests

Unit tests in `loader_test.go` list the loader cases side by side.
Acceptance tests under `acceptance/bundle/strict_profile_match/` cover
the same rules end to end, including `--profile`, `workspace.profile`,
`default_profile` and the behavior without the variable. Accepted cases
print the auth a bundle script receives, which shows the selected
profile and host.

Update Go SDK to v0.189.0 (#7138)

This PR updates the Go SDK dependency and generates APIs from that
release's OpenAPI specification.

---------

Co-authored-by: databricks-ci-ghec-2[bot] <184307802+databricks-ci-ghec-2[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Jan Rose 
Co-authored-by: Isaac

Backward incompatibility

  • Dropped support for Python 3.10. Snowflake CLI requires Python 3.11, 3.12, or 3.13.

Deprecations

New additions

  • Streamlit entities support include_project_definition: true to opt in to uploading the project-root snowflake.yml with snow streamlit deploy. When that file is uploaded, deploy emits a warning because stage readers can retrieve it.
  • snow upgrade is now generally available. It upgrades a direct install of Snowflake CLI and is listed in snow --help without a feature flag. Other install channels refuse and print the direct-install command.
  • snow sql accepts !spool and !spool off. Subsequent query results are appended to the file and still printed on the terminal. Until !spool off, TABLE is a static pipe table on both the terminal and the file: no Live refresh and no wrapping to the window. Format follows --format / !set output_format.
  • snow sql accepts !set output_format= (plain, table, json, json_ext, csv). plain prints query results without box drawing. --format PLAIN selects the same layout.
  • A Streamlit entity in snowflake.yml accepts five settings that Snowsight Workspaces writes, and snow streamlit deploy applies them. execute_as (OWNER or RESTRICTED CALLER) and app_warehouse apply to SYSTEM$WAREHOUSE_RUNTIME. A container runtime always uses OWNER and ignores app_warehouse with a warning. artifact_repositories and schedules apply to container runtimes. idle_auto_shutdown_time_seconds applies to each runtime. schedules (cron_exprs, maximum 5, and timezone, default UTC) makes one warm-up task for each expression, named __STREAMLIT_LIFECYCLE[_n]. A deploy changes only the tasks that are different. An empty cron_exprs drops the tasks. An empty artifact_repositories removes the repositories. The tasks need CREATE TASK, EXECUTE TASK, and EXECUTE MANAGED TASK, and DROP STREAMLIT does not drop them. If snowflake.yml does not set a value, the live value does not change. A setting on the incorrect runtime, or on a --legacy deploy, stops the deploy before the first SQL. Earlier CLI versions do not accept these keys.

Fixes and improvements

  • snow streamlit deploy --replace now applies main_file changes to existing versioned apps in place, preserving the app, grants and version history. Files are uploaded before the entrypoint changes; --prune runs only after the change succeeds. Accounts that reject the update receive an actionable error.
  • Streamlit deploy now refuses to recreate an existing app with no live stage unless a legacy ROOT_LOCATION is known, and rejects --prune with an unset main_file when the active entrypoint is absent from the bundle.
  • Upgraded the Python interpreter embedded in Linux binaries from 3.10.22 to 3.12.15. macOS and Windows binaries now embed Python 3.12 as well.
  • Bumped lower bound of certifi to 2026.10.19.
  • The direct install script restricts connections.toml and config.toml to the current user when that user owns the file. snow upgrade does the same before it checks permissions, and again before it points at the new version, so a file left readable by other accounts no longer stops snow upgrade or the new snow from starting. Symlinks and files owned by someone else are left unchanged.
  • Upgraded pip from 26.2.1 to 26.2.2.

v3.30.0

Backward incompatibility

  • Re-running snow helpers import-snowsql-connections can save a different connection than an earlier import. Custom --snowsql-config-file paths are merged after the default SnowSQL files instead of replacing that list, and /usr/lib64/snowflake/snowsql/config is read last when it exists. Named connections are saved from connections. alone and do not receive keys from the unnamed [connections] section. login_timeout, client_session_keep_alive, ocsp_fail_open, insecure_mode, and client_store_temporary_credential are copied from [options] when a connection omits them; a key set on the connection wins. Passwords and other text stay strings, including values that look like numbers. login_timeout and client_prefetch_threads are saved as integers, and client_session_keep_alive, client_store_temporary_credential, ocsp_fail_open, insecure_mode, oauth_disable_pkce, oauth_enable_refresh_tokens, oauth_enable_single_use_refresh_tokens, and disable_request_pooling are saved as booleans. default_connection_name is set only from the unnamed [connections] section, under the name it was actually saved with. When WORKSPACE is set, .snowsql.cnf and .snowsql/config are read from that directory instead of the home directory.
  • snow streamlit deploy no longer defaults query_warehouse to the identifier streamlit when the field is omitted from snowflake.yml. A new app uses the connection warehouse instead, and deploy fails if that is also unset. An existing app keeps its warehouse unless snowflake.yml sets query_warehouse.
  • snow streamlit deploy --replace now UNSETs Streamlit properties (title, comment, external access integrations, secrets, imports, compute_pool) that were cleared from snowflake.yml, and REVOKEs object grants that disappeared from grants: (OWNERSHIP is left alone). Omitting grants: still leaves live grants untouched. If the app's current grants cannot be listed, deploy fails rather than skip the revoke.

Deprecations

New additions

  • snow feature is now generally available. This command group manages declarative feature-store objects in Snowflake (init, sync, plan, apply, list, describe, online-service (status/create/drop), ingest, query). It is now visible by default and no longer requires the ENABLE_FEATURE_STORE feature flag. It requires the snowflake-ml-python[feature_store] library.
  • Air-gapped mode configures the CLI for isolated environments that cannot reach the public internet. Enable it with cli.air_gapped in config.toml or SNOWFLAKE_CLI_AIR_GAPPED. The environment variable is read at runtime and is not copied into a newly created config.toml. Commands that talk to external services may change or refuse to run, including PyPI and Homebrew version checks, snow upgrade, auto-upgrade, snow init against the public GitHub template default, and pip-backed flows such as snow snowpark build. Pip in those flows uses --isolated and only --index-url or PIP_INDEX_URL. When air-gapped mode is set, Snowsight no longer falls back to app.snowflake.com. Override remaining defaults with cli.per_account_app_domain in config.toml or SNOWFLAKE_CLI_PER_ACCOUNT_APP_DOMAIN, and with SNOWFLAKE_AUDIENCE for GitHub OIDC.
  • Override the default snow init template repository with cli.init_template_source in config.toml or SNOWFLAKE_CLI_INIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE. Air-gapped mode requires this override, a local --template-source, or an in-region git URL.
  • snow dcm plan and snow dcm deploy now accept --deployment to plan or deploy from an existing deployment, by name or alias, instead of uploading local files. The deployment is used as stored: the manifest target's configuration and environment variables are not applied again. --variable and --env-file cannot be combined with --deployment.

Fixes and improvements

  • Connection diagnostics and the per-account cert probe now require TLS 1.3. snow init --template-source, SQL !source/!load, and pip index URLs reject plaintext http://.
  • snow app version drop now reports that the drop is in progress and may take a few minutes, instead of saying it is already complete.
  • Upgraded setuptools from 80.8.0 to 84.0.0.
  • Comparing an FQN against a value that is not an FQN instance now returns False instead of raising AttributeError.
  • Upgraded keyring from 25.6.0 to 25.7.0.
  • Upgraded jaraco.context from 6.0.1 to 6.1.2.
  • snow streamlit deploy includes environment.yml and the pages directory (pages_dir, or pages/ by default) when they exist on disk, even if a native v2 project lists only main_file in artifacts. Overlapping pages/ and pages/*.py artifacts no longer fail the bundle.
  • snow streamlit deploy treats only Snowflake error 2003 from DESCRIBE STREAMLIT as "object does not exist". Other programming errors are no longer swallowed into a misleading CREATE STREAMLIT IF NOT EXISTS. Because 2003 also means "not authorized", --replace no longer turns it into CREATE OR REPLACE.
  • Improved sanitization of external access integration and secret values in generated Streamlit and Snowpark SQL, and of import and stage location values in generated Streamlit SQL. imports, external_access_integrations, secrets, runtime_name, and compute_pool in snowflake.yml no longer accept a backslash.
  • snow streamlit get-url and the URL printed after deploy now fail when the connection has no account or region, instead of opening https://app.snowflake.com with no app path.
  • snow streamlit logs accepts any SYSTEM$ST_CONTAINER_RUNTIME* runtime, matching deploy/restart. A newer container runtime such as ..._PY3_12 is also accepted in snowflake.yml.
  • Replacing a legacy ROOT_LOCATION Streamlit app with a versioned deploy copies files from the old stage onto the new versioned stage when possible.
  • ALTER STREAMLIT ... ADD LIVE VERSION quotes each database, schema, and name part so hyphenated or reserved identifiers parse.
  • snow helpers import-snowsql-connections reads SnowSQL files the way SnowSQL 1.5 does: quotes are removed, # starts a comment, and the file is decoded as UTF-8. A repeated collision while naming the unnamed [connections] section stops after three tries instead of prompting forever.
  • snow helpers import-snowsql-connections keeps a private-key passphrase from the SnowSQL file, adds authenticator = "SNOWFLAKE_JWT" when a private key is imported and authenticator is still absent after the files are merged, and preserves region and proxy settings for the connector. The short SnowSQL key wins over a long alias across files. A blank or whitespace short key is skipped, so the next alias is used. private_key_path wins over private_key_file when both are present. A blank value is omitted, so a later blank clears an earlier value. When the authenticator that survives the merge is present and is not SNOWFLAKE_JWT, the private key and passphrase are omitted. A SnowSQL file that exists but cannot be opened, cannot be decoded, or is not valid INI fails the import before anything is written. The message names the path and does not repeat the file contents. A section with no remaining values is not saved.
  • snow helpers check-snowsql-env-vars reports the SnowSQL variable that is actually set. SNOWSQL_REGION suggests putting the account identifier in SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT, not the region name. The deprecated proxy variables are suggested as the host, port, username, or password inside HTTPS_PROXY or HTTP_PROXY.
  • The direct install script updates the bash startup file the shell reads. It edits the first existing login profile (~/.bash_profile, ~/.bash_login, or ~/.profile) and an existing ~/.bashrc, and does not create a bash login profile.
  • A configuration file with permissions that are too open now prints the chmod or icacls command on its own line. Copying that command no longer includes a line break or the error box border.
  • Upgraded GitPython from 3.1.62 to 3.2.0.
