feat: [SNOW-4138413] add snow sql !spool

### Pre-review checklist
   * [x] If my changes add or modify user-facing interface (commands, flags, output formats), I consulted maintainers and got sign-off beforehand ([how](https://github.com/snowflakedb/snowflake-cli/blob/main/docs/contributing/adding-commands.md#design-sign-off-before-writing-code)).
   * [x] I've confirmed that instructions included in README.md are still correct after my changes in the codebase.
   * [x] I've added or updated unit tests to verify correctness of my new code.
   * [x] I've added or updated integration tests to verify correctness of my new code.
   * [x] Manually tested on macOS
   * [ ] Manually tested on Windows
   * [x] I've confirmed my changes are up-to-date with the target branch.
   * [x] I've described my changes in `RELEASE-NOTES.md` (see [when and how](https://github.com/snowflakedb/snowflake-cli/blob/main/docs/contributing/lifecycle.md#release-notes-format)).
   * [x] I've updated documentation if behavior changed.

### Changes description
Adds SnowSQL-compatible `!spool ` / `!spool off` ([SNOW-4138413](https://snowflakecomputing.atlassian.net/browse/SNOW-4138413)).

`!spool` opens the path for append (UTF-8, `~` expanded). Later `print_result` output is written to that file **and** still printed on the terminal until `!spool off`. Format follows `--format` / `!set output_format`. Works in the REPL, `-q`, and `-f`. The whole remainder is one path (spaces and `=` allowed). `off` is a case-insensitive keyword, so a file named `off` cannot be spooled. Success is silent. `!spool off` when already off is a no-op.

The file is the formatted query result only (TABLE / PLAIN / JSON / CSV). Prompts, `!` commands, SQL text, and `Time Elapsed` stay on the terminal.

A new spool file is owner-only (`0600`). Appending to an existing file leaves its mode unchanged and warns if others can read or write it. On Windows the same warning uses `file_permissions_are_strict()`. A missing `whoami`/`icacls` does not abort `!spool`. The path is sanitized before the warning and the unwritable-path error.

Until `!spool off`, TABLE is a static pipe table on both sinks (no Live refresh, no wrapping to the window).

#### SnowSQL 1.5.2 vs `snow sql`

Replicated from SnowSQL `!spool`:

| | SnowSQL 1.5.2 | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What is in the file | Formatted query result only | Same (`print_result` only) |
| Still printed on the terminal | Yes | Yes |
| Prompts, SQL, `!` commands, timing / row counts in the file | No (default) | No |
| Append, not overwrite | Yes | Yes |
| REPL, `-q`, `-f` | Yes | Yes |

Intentionally different:

| | SnowSQL 1.5.2 | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New file mode | Usually `0644` (umask) | `0600` |
| Existing file broader than owner-only | Silent | Warn; mode unchanged |
| TABLE on screen while spooling | Always static tabulate | Static pipe table so it matches the file (CLI otherwise uses Live / wrap on a TTY) |
| Format names | Tabulate (`psql`, `csv`, …) | `--format` / `!set` (`table`, `plain`, `json`, …) |
| No-args / unwritable path | `The file is not writeable:` | CLI usage / `Cannot write spool file` |
| `output_file`, `timing_in_output_file`, `!print` | Exists | Out of scope |

#### Errors vs SnowSQL 1.5.2

| Case | SnowSQL 1.5.2 | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no args | `The file is not writeable:` (empty path) | `No arguments passed to 'spool' command. Usage: !spool  or !spool off` |
| unwritable path | `The file is not writeable: ` | `Cannot write spool file '': ` |
| `off` when already off | silent | silent |

#### Why tee through `print_result`, not `sys.stdout =`
Query results are consumed once. Tee at write time via `_result_stream()` to `TeeTextIO` so JSON, CSV, TABLE, and PLAIN all hit both sinks without rendering twice.

Do not assign `sys.stdout`. Rich caches `is_terminal` on the stream it first saw (`_stdout_is_terminal` / GH#2725). While spooling, both sinks use the non-TTY layout so the file does not pick up ANSI / Live.

#### Single-SELECT print order
For one SELECT, Typer prints after `execute_sql` returns. Draining the statement generator first would run `!spool off` before `print_result`, so the file would be empty. The one-SELECT path prints `QueryResult` from `next()`, drains the rest (including `!spool off`), then returns `EmptyResult()`. A trailing `!set` after a single SELECT does not rewrite that result.

#### Why not public [PR #2721](https://github.com/snowflakedb/snowflake-cli/pull/2721)
REPL-only; truncates; `sys.stdout =`; extra `-- Query:` banner. Wrong contract for this ticket.

Out of scope: SnowSQL `output_file` / `timing_in_output_file`, overwrite flag, spooling prompts or Time Elapsed.

## Test plan
- [x] Unit: spool create `0600`; warn on existing `0644` / `0640` / `0666` / `0622`; no warn on existing `0600`; trailing `!set` after a single SELECT stays TABLE
- [x] Unit: Windows owner-only warning (not skipped); `CliError` from the permission check does not abort; ANSI stripped from the warning and `Cannot write spool file`
- [x] Integration: `tests_integration/sql/test_snowsql_commands.py` spool cases
- [x] Manual, macOS, PR worktree `hatch run snow sql`: `select repeat('x', 400)` wraps; after `!spool` the same query is one long line on screen and in the file; after `!spool off` wrap returns
- [x] Manual, SnowSQL 1.5.2: REPL `!spool /tmp/snowsql-spool-contents.txt` then `select 2 as n;` — file is only the table. `-q` with newlines (`!spool` / `select 4` / `!spool off`) — file is only the table. `!spool path; select …` on one line is one `!spool` and creates no file

* fix(fmt): keep code before `{%-` tags; make parser iteration limit a per-file error

Reflow indents through the placeholder a trimming `{%-` tag leaves for the
newline it swallowed. `ReflowPoint::indent_to` measured the current indent
from the placeholder's `source_str`, which an earlier pass had already
rewritten, but subtracted it from the original source slice. On the second
pass the source fix grew backwards over the code before the tag, so
`b.user_id` became `b.user`. Measure against the original source text.

The sqlfluffrs parser panics when it exceeds its iteration budget, and the
CLI panic hook exits the process, so one large file aborted `dbt fmt` for
every file. Add `dbt_common::panic::catch_unwind_quietly`, which the CLI hook
honours, and use it around the format parse so the file fails with
SyntaxInvalid. Format parse errors now carry the file path as their location.
Also pass `rust_parser_max_iterations` from `.sqlfluff` through to the parser.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5

description:
Change all HTTP or HTTP-wrapping crates to use only the OS certificate store

* dbt-adbc: use the OS certificate store for Snowflake OAuth token refresh

The refresh-token agent had no TLS config, so ureq fell back to its
bundled webpki roots and failed behind TLS-intercepting proxies whose CA
is only in the OS store. Reuse install::build_tls_config(), as driver
downloads already do.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 

* dbt-auth: use the OS certificate store for Azure Databricks tenant discovery

The ureq agent behind discover_azure_tenant_id had no TLS config, so it
trusted only ureq's bundled webpki roots. Use
dbt_adbc::install::build_tls_config() so it verifies against the OS store.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 

* dbt-adapter: use the OS certificate store for the Databricks Python model API client

The ureq agent that submits Databricks Python models had no TLS config,
so it trusted only ureq's bundled webpki roots. Use
dbt_adbc::install::build_tls_config() so it verifies against the OS store.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 

* dbt-onboard: use the OS certificate store when downloading AGENTS.md files

ureq::get() uses the default agent, which trusts only ureq's bundled
webpki roots. Build an agent with RootCerts::PlatformVerifier instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 

* vortex-client: default to the OS certificate store

VortexEnv::tls_config() returned None by default, so every host except
dbt-index sent telemetry through ureq's bundled webpki roots. Default to
a RootCerts::PlatformVerifier config instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 

* Use the OS certificate store for reqwest in the root workspace

The workspace reqwest dependency enabled rustls-tls, which trusts the
bundled webpki roots. Switch it to rustls-tls-native-roots so reqwest
clients verify against the OS certificate store.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 

* sdf-slt: stop gcp-bigquery-client from enabling bundled webpki roots

gcp-bigquery-client's default rust-tls feature turns on reqwest's
rustls-tls, and hakari unified that into workspace-hack, so every crate's
reqwest client trusted the bundled webpki roots next to the OS store.
Disable its default features and keep gzip and ring; reqwest gets rustls
with native roots from the workspace features. Regenerate workspace-hack.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 

* flock-service: use the OS certificate store for reqwest

Switch the identify-service reqwest client from rustls-tls (bundled
webpki roots) to rustls-tls-native-roots.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 

* wizard-app: use the OS certificate store for reqwest

Switch the Tauri backend's reqwest client from rustls-tls (bundled
webpki roots) to rustls-tls-native-roots, matching the codex crates it
already links.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 

* Add changelog entries for using the OS certificate store

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 

* hakari: keep z3-sys's bundled-roots reqwest feature out of workspace-hack

z3 is a macOS-only sdf-slt dependency whose z3-sys build script
downloads z3 with reqwest/rustls-tls. Hakari unified that host-only
feature into the aarch64-apple-darwin target dependencies, so local
macOS builds linked reqwest with the bundled webpki roots again.
Exclude z3-sys from hakari's traversal and regenerate workspace-hack.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 

* dbt-auth-tests: use the OS certificate store for OAuth token requests

The Snowflake and Databricks OAuth helpers called ureq::post(), whose
default agent trusts only ureq's bundled webpki roots. Build an agent
with dbt_adbc::install::build_tls_config() instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 

* Drop ureq's bundled webpki roots

The workspace ureq dependency enabled the `rustls` feature, which links
webpki-roots and makes RootCerts::WebPki the default for any agent without
a TLS config. Enable `rustls-no-provider` + `_ring` + `platform-verifier`
instead: same rustls and ring crypto, but no bundled roots, so an agent
that forgets to select RootCerts::PlatformVerifier panics instead of
silently trusting the bundled CA list.

webpki-roots is now absent from the runtime dependency graph on Linux,
macOS and Windows; it remains only behind z3-sys's macOS build script.

Ban webpki-root-certs alongside webpki-roots so neither bundled Mozilla
CA list can reach dbt-cli. Limit the cargo-deny graph to the platforms
dbt-cli ships for: rustls-platform-verifier depends on
webpki-root-certs only on wasm32, which has no OS certificate store.

feat(competitions): add --public to competitions leaderboard (#1222)

## Summary

`leaderboard --show` and `--download` return different leaderboards on a
concluded competition, and neither says which. This adds `--public` so
the public leaderboard is reachable from `--show`.

## Problem

`--show` calls `GetLeaderboard`, whose `override_public` field the CLI
never set, so it returns the final leaderboard. `--download` calls
`DownloadLeaderboard`, which has no such field and returns the public
one. On `playground-series-s6e8`:

```text
--show                          --download
0.97176  Chris Deotte           0.97207  Chris Deotte
0.97123  MILANFX                0.97154  Changye Li
0.97120  Changye Li             0.97149  MILANFX
```

Ranks 2 and 3 swap, and further down the two lists hold different teams.
Measurements for three competitions are on #731.

## Solution

`--public` sets `override_public` on the `GetLeaderboard` request:

```bash
kaggle competitions leaderboard playground-series-s6e8 --show --public
```

```text
  teamId  teamName      submissionDate              score
--------  ------------  --------------------------  -------
16724329  Chris Deotte  2026-08-30 23:14:31.186000  0.97207
16698321  Changye Li    2026-08-30 12:49:14.556000  0.97154
16633740  MILANFX       2026-08-31 23:53:41.770000  0.97149
```

which is what `--download` gives.

The field is only set when the flag is passed, so without it the request
is what it was and `--show` still returns the final leaderboard. I left
that default alone because it is what the competition page shows by
default once a competition has concluded.

`--download` is unchanged, and `--public` does not reach it.

The help text and `docs/competitions.md` now say which leaderboard each
flag returns. Both previously described a difference in destination
only, which is what makes this easy to miss.

## On `--download`

It still cannot return the final leaderboard. That needs either
`override_public` added to the `DownloadLeaderboard` request, which is a
kagglesdk and server change rather than a CLI one, or serving
`--download` by paging `GetLeaderboard`. The second stays in this repo
but costs one request per 200 rows, and those rows carry only `team_id`,
`team_name`, `submission_date` and `score`, so the CSV would lose the
`Rank`, `SubmissionCount` and `TeamMemberUserNames` columns the server
writes today. Asked on #731 instead of picking one.

## Testing

- [x] `hatch -e test run pytest tests/unit` (1408 passed, 3 skipped)
- [x] `hatch run lint:all`
- [x] Live against the API: `--show --public` matches `--download` on
`playground-series-s6e8`, `--show` on its own is unchanged, and on the
running `arc-prize-2026-arc-agi-2` both forms return the same rows
- [ ] Maintainer: please run `/gcbrun` when convenient

Eight new tests cover the flag setting the field, the default leaving
the request alone, paging still applying alongside it, the CLI
forwarding the flag, and `--public` not altering the download call.
Seven of the eight fail against the previous code. The one that does not
is the regression guard on the no-flag request, which has to pass either
way. One existing parser test gained an assertion that `public` defaults
to False.

## Related

Part of #731. It does not close it, since the `--download` half is still
open.

Require certifi >= 2026.10.19 for the emSign/eMudhra CA compromise (#1227)

certifi releases before 2026.10.19 trust the compromised emSign/eMudhra
roots (GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2), so a MITM could forge a kaggle.com cert and
steal API tokens. #1223 pinned certifi only in requirements.lock and
tools/releases/requirements.txt, which pip ignores for
`pip install kaggle`. kaggle pulled certifi only via requests, which
sets no floor, so existing installs could keep a vulnerable bundle.

This adds the floor to the published dependencies, and refreshes the OS
ca-certificates and pip in the CI image, mirroring Kaggle/kagglehub#318
and Kaggle/kaggle-sdk-python#75.

Fixes #1202 (follow-up to #1201).

## Problem
`kernels_delete` in `src/kaggle/api/kaggle_api_extended.py` did
`owner_slug, kernel_slug = kernel.split("/")`, so `kaggle kernels delete
owner/slug/3` crashed with `ValueError: too many values to unpack
(expected 2)`.

Parse with `parse_kernel_string()` (same helper the version-aware
commands from #1201 use) and explicitly reject a version, mirroring
`dataset_delete_cli` (#1194):
- `owner/slug/3` and `owner/slug/v3` raise `ValueError: Deleting
individual kernel versions is not supported (specified version: ...). To
delete the entire kernel, run: kaggle kernels delete owner/slug`
- trailing slash `owner/slug/` is tolerated like datasets delete
- bare `slug` resolves via configured user through
`parse_kernel_string`, consistent with other kernel commands

## Testing

version, no-confirm, success asserts `user_name`/`kernel_slug`, trailing
slash, None)

passed
- `test_kernel_versions + pull/push/logs/output/paths/parsing`: 82
passed

fix(tooling): stop flagging caller-compatible changes as API breakage (#824)

* fix(tooling): stop flagging caller-compatible changes as API breakage

compare_api_breakage.py reported several changes that cannot break a
caller:

- Return types: a subclass of the old type (Account -> AccountExtended),
  also inside covariant generic arguments (List, Iterator, Mapping, ...),
  now counts as narrowed. Callable and Generator/Coroutine arguments
  still need an exact match. A top-level Any/object return narrowed to a
  concrete type is compatible too.
- A None-only return that gains a value is compatible: type checkers
  reject using a None result, so callers could only discard it.
- AexPy's AddOptionalParameter is ranked breaking only for subclass
  overrides; SDK clients are used rather than subclassed, so it counts as
  compatible.

Dropping RawData (dict[str, Any]) or List[RawData] stays breaking at any
nesting level. Compatible findings are listed only under --verbose
(VERBOSE=1), like the other compatible lists.

核心通过注册项选择授权实现，具体 SDK 由 overlay 提供。
服务地址使用系统统一的 MCP 配置（mcp_url 文件或默认地址），登录不修改端点配置。

Overlay 接入

公共类型位于 pkg/edition，overlay 不需要也不得导入核心的 internal/auth。
在已有 NewHooks() 中注册名称及授权回调，再沿用启动入口的 edition.Override(h)：

h.OIDCProviders = func() []edition.OIDCProvider {
    return []edition.OIDCProvider{
        {
            Name:      "ant",
            Authorize: authorizeWithAntSDK,
        },
    }
}

authorizeWithAntSDK 的函数签名为：

func(context.Context, edition.OIDCAuthorizationRequest) (edition.OIDCAuthorizationResult, error)

蚂蚁适配负责调用自己的 SDK，并把 SDK 实际返回的 code/state 转为公共结果类型。
若已有 AuthorizeOIDC 使用业务侧 DTO，只在这个回调中转换类型；不用复制核心事务、
换票或保存凭证代码。SDK 初始化与认证发生在回调执行时，注册函数只返回声明。
名称可由 overlay 自定义，但必须满足 [a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}，并与 Portal 已配置的
provider 一致。重复名称、空回调、非法名称均为注册错误。

执行边界

  1. 核心校验 CLI 参数并选择已注册的回调。
  2. 核心向 Portal 创建事务，校验服务端 provider、授权参数与有效期。
  3. 核心向回调传入 authorization_endpoint、独立的参数 map 及受事务期限约束的 context。
  4. SDK 尊重取消与超时，原样使用服务端授权参数并返回实际取得的 code/state。
  5. 核心验证授权码及原事务 state，再换票、补全身份、保存 DWS profile。

SDK 会话、密码、DWS 换票用的 client secret 和 PKCE verifier 不属于这个回调的输入输出。
错误中不得包含认证材料；核心也不记录 SDK 原始错误文本。授权失败、取消、超时或
state 不匹配不会触发其他 SDK 或 Mock 兜底，也不会换票或保存凭证。

没有注册对应实现时，核心仍先检查 Portal 配置；服务端接受 provider 后返回
OIDC_SDK_UNAVAILABLE。Help 和 dry-run 不枚举注册项、不初始化 SDK、不访问网络。
普通 OAuth/PAT 登录和分步 exchange-prepare / token-exchange 入口保持独立。

联调与依赖更新

核心的 Hook API 提交并推送后，overlay 需要把远程核心依赖更新到包含该 API 的提交，
再编译上述注册代码。只修改另一 Go 包里的同名文件不会替换核心实现。

回归验证覆盖自定义名称和 ant 注册、真实命令入口及凭证保存、非法/重复/缺失注册、
后端拒绝、SDK 错误脱敏、取消/超时、state 篡改、空授权码和 help/dry-run 无副作用。

DWS_PACKAGE_VERSION=0.0.0-test CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./pkg/edition ./internal/auth ./internal/app

已验证：上述三个包的完整测试、Hook 定向 race 测试、go vet ./...、make build，
以及构建后二进制的 provider-login help / dry-run。未执行真实蚂蚁网关登录。

  • 支持业务分步完成第三方登录：先执行 dws auth exchange-prepare --provider ant 获取服务端授权参数，再由业务调用 IdP/SDK 取码，最后执行 dws auth token-exchange --provider ant --code --state 换取 DWS Token。

支持 --code-stdin、可选且必须成对的 --client-id/--client-secret，默认返回现有 TokenData；显式 --save 后在线核验完整身份并保存，保留已有默认账号。两个命令均支持 --dry-run，服务地址使用系统统一的 MCP 配置（mcp_url 文件或默认地址），不修改全局配置；保存 Token 时记录其刷新所用的 Portal 地址。PKCE verifier 始终由服务端保存，换票失败不会自动重试一次性 code/state。

命令沿用统一结果输出。作为第三方 IdP 集成入口，两个命令以 Cobra Hidden 隐藏，不出现在 dws auth --help 与 shell 补全中，仍可显式执行；不进入 Agent Schema（Hidden 且无 Contract.Identity），也不再占用 reviewed Schema 排除列表。

macOS 终端按实际文件描述符识别，使用 select 等待输入，不依赖 /dev/tty 或 /dev/stdin 文件名，覆盖 < /dev/tty 重定向；以 50ms 周期检查取消，不改变终端模式、不关闭借用句柄。高编号输入使用低编号描述符副本等待，完成后只关闭副本；低编号描述符耗尽时明确报错。

--code-stdin 的等待输入和后续换票共享一分钟超时，并响应调用方的取消或更短截止时间。取消、超时错误保留原有身份，不归类为参数错误，也不会继续换票。Unix 标准输入使用可取消的轮询读取，取消后保留原文件描述符；Windows 控制台保留原输入模式，通过原生 API 取消读取，重定向管道则通过关闭来中断。宿主通过 SetIn 注入的自定义阻塞输入须支持 Close 中断读取（取消时会关闭，正常完成时保留）。无 Close 的自定义 Reader 须为非阻塞或自行响应 context。

OIDC 换票响应增加实际 DWS clientId（与 IdP 的 client_id 不同）。provider-login 和 token-exchange --save 均保存该应用绑定和原 Portal 地址。默认应用继续由 Portal 托管密钥；显式指定的自定义应用将原始密钥保存到现有安全凭证槽，并与 Token/Profile 写入一起回滚。刷新自定义应用时从该槽读取密钥，发送给原 Portal 的 /oauth2/refreshToken，不回退到全局应用、不跟随重定向、不在结果或 app.json 中暴露密钥。未使用 --save 的分步换票不写入本地凭证。

需要同步部署 Portal：默认 OIDC 响应返回实际 clientId，刷新接口接受可选 clientSecret。旧版默认响应缺少应用绑定时，新 CLI 会明确要求更新 Portal；旧的缺失绑定记录需要重新登录。

OIDC 登录持久化时记录 oidc_provider，刷新成功继续保留；该本地元数据不加入未保存的 token-exchange 返回值。所有 OIDC 分支只通过该字段识别，不再从 Portal 地址或密钥模式推断登录来源。此前未记录该字段的开发测试凭证不做兼容迁移，需重新登录。

OIDC 刷新前校验原应用、Portal 和登录来源绑定，缺失时直接报错，不使用全局应用或默认端点兜底。刷新失败不读取组织镜像或历史全局凭证，即使同用户、同组织也不能切换应用。被拒绝或失效时提示重新执行 provider-login 或原分步登录流程，自定义应用需沿用原 client-id/client-secret；网络、取消、超时、限流和 5xx 保留原凭证，不强制重新登录。普通 OAuth 既有恢复策略保持不变。

已确认的 invalidParameter.authCode.notFound 仍保留脱敏后的错误类型和规范化业务码供分类使用；错误识别不再意味着允许 OIDC 凭证恢复。服务端原始错误文本不进入输出、日志或错误链。

Fixed

  • Installer skill failures (#779) — fail explicitly without an installation-success banner when a release archive has no usable skills and no local source is available; also fail when the PowerShell local mono skill directory is missing.

  • 修复 Gitee 补同步入口遗漏 OpenHarmony 附件的问题，使已发布稳定版本的完整九项制品能够通过附件清单校验。

description:
[v1.0.19] - 2026-10-20

Added

  • New hidden subcommand auth exchange-code (cmd/auth/exchange_code.go, cmd/auth/base.go): Exchanges the current CLI login session for a short-lived, one-time authorization code issued by the Open Platform, intended for upstream callers' backends to resolve the user's identity.
  • Comprehensive unit tests for internal/output/print_test.go (524 lines): Covers the five core functions marshalNoEscape, PrintInfof, PrintErrorf, FormatPrint, and GetFormat. Primarily locks in the literal-% regression fixed in the "Changed" section below, and explicitly asserts that: error messages must route through cmd.ErrOrStderr() and must not be diverted onto stdout by SetOut; FormatPrint does not escape < / > / &; an unknown --format value falls back to compact JSON; empty trace_id / message are elided via omitempty; and the WithHints option correctly injects the hints field.

Changed

  • PrintInfof / PrintErrorf no longer format format when no variadic args are provided (internal/output/print.go): The previous implementation always went through fmt.Sprintf(format, args...) regardless of whether args was supplied. When callers passed an already-assembled string as the sole argument (e.g. one containing 50%, URL-encoded %20 / %2F, or a server-returned error description), fmt.Sprintf interpreted those % characters as format verbs lacking arguments, leaking artefacts such as %!x(MISSING) / %!(MISSING) into the output. Both functions now branch explicitly: when len(args) == 0 the format string is printed verbatim; otherwise it is still fed through fmt.Sprintf. This keeps both "pass a complete sentence" and "pass a printf-style template" call styles correct.
  • PrintErrorf now writes to cmd.ErrOrStderr(), and the cmd == nil branch uses fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, ...) (internal/output/print.go): It previously used cmd.OutOrStderr(), which is overridden by SetOut — so when a caller set only SetOut (e.g. piping stdout into a buffer for structured consumption), error messages were incorrectly interleaved into the stdout stream and polluted agents' JSON parsing of business data. Switching to ErrOrStderr() guarantees error output stays strictly on the error stream, consistent with the long-standing convention that "stdout carries business data, stderr carries diagnostics". The cmd == nil branch is likewise moved from fmt.Printf to fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, ...) so it also routes through stderr.

Review follow-up.

The access guidance moves from tryMessage to nextSteps. `store create dev --json` and `store delete --json` only serialize message and nextSteps, so the guidance on which access to grant and where was lost from their JSON output. Command tests now cover both JSON paths.

withOrganizationStoreAccess, which each call site had to remember to wrap around its request, is replaced by organizationStoresRequestDoc in @shopify/organizations. It sends a Business Platform Organizations API request for an organization and turns a refused one into OrganizationStoreAccessError. Every Organizations API request in the store and organizations packages now goes through it: store list, store create dev and its creation poll, store delete and its confirmation poll, and the shop lookup behind store info and store delete. A new request gets the same handling by using the helper.

Drop unused re-exports and keep app dev's 401 message

Knip failed on the two names the store package re-exported from @shopify/organizations but never imports: isOrganizationAccessError and OrganizationStoreAccessError. The store commands only use withOrganizationStoreAccess.

cli-kit now reports a 401 that survives the token refresh as an error with a statusCode instead of a raw graphql-request ClientError. app dev's upload step caught that shape with a bare `Error('Unauthorized')`, which would have replaced its "Auth session expired. Please run `shopify app dev` again." message. It now raises that same AbortError, and a test covers it.

description:
Explain a token's missing dev store access instead of dumping the 401

An app-only service account token running `store list`, `store create dev`
or `store delete` crashed the CLI with the raw graphql-request error for
Business Platform's 401: the full query text and variables, plus a stack
trace, presented as a CLI bug.

Two things were wrong. cli-kit's GraphQL client hands a 401 back raw so
the caller's token refresh can run, but when the refreshed request was
rejected too (or there was nothing to refresh) that raw error escaped,
skipping the error handler every other failed response goes through. The
client now maps a final 401 through that handler, unless the caller asked
for raw errors with `handleErrors: false`, and the handler no longer tries
to quote a GraphQL body a gateway's 401 doesn't have.

On top of that, the store commands now say what the 401 means. The
Organizations API refuses a token that holds no organization scope, which
for a service account means it has no dev store access. A new
`withOrganizationStoreAccess` helper in @shopify/organizations turns that
refusal into an error naming the credential and where to fix it: the
service account's Dev store management access under Settings > Users >
Security, a service account token in place of a legacy automation token,
or the user's own permission. `store list`, `store create dev` and
`store delete` use it.

Co-authored-by: Eddie Gao
product_or_resource: Explain a token's missing dev store access instead of dumping the 401

Fix theme profile for URLs with a query string and report redirects

Split the --url into a path and a query before rendering. The renderer appends its own query, so a --url with a query string produced a malformed URL that dropped _fd=0, and stores with a custom primary domain answered with a 301. Reject a --url that can't be parsed, or that starts with //, instead of crashing or profiling another page.

Raise an AbortError with the redirect destination when the profiled page redirects. Only suggest a new --url when it differs from the requested one, flag destinations on other hosts, and point to --store-password for /password. Raise an AbortError for other non-200 responses too, so they are reported as expected errors instead of crashes.

Minor Changes

    Fetch and follow the instructions at https://docs.slack.dev/agent-setup/prompt.md

  • 42ad160: Add the deploy-slack-app skill: deploy a Socket Mode Bolt app to Railway or Heroku as a separate, always-on Slack app with its own app ID, using the Slack CLI deploy hook. The local development app is unchanged. Supports macOS and Linux, with Windows support planned.

Patch Changes

  • 2118120: Support basic developer sandboxes, now that every Developer Program account can create one with no paid plan or payment method. create-slack-app says so when recommending a sandbox, explains a basic sandbox's limits and how to upgrade it, and checks that the logged-in email matches the developer's account before sending them to sign up.
  • 96f6ea2: Add design references to the block-kit skill for modals and forms, App Home, data display (fields, tables, and charts), agent progress (plans and task cards), and human-in-the-loop approvals. Extend the design principles to cover data_table, data_visualization, container, alert, and inline tag, date, and citation elements. Fix the Notification Alert pattern, which used the modal-only alert block in a message.
    Align labels in the guidance and patterns with Slack's UI conventions (Title Case action buttons, sentence case elsewhere, no emoji in buttons, labels, or headers), and limit primary styling to one button per message or view.
  • faf8b3a: Fix create-slack-app never handing off to the block-kit skill, so an agent building a message, modal, or App Home layout now uses it instead of writing Block Kit JSON from memory. create-slack-app and block-kit also check their optional argument against the allowed values before using it, and ask the developer when it doesn't match.
  • faf8b3a: Clarify in the block-kit skill that blocks.validate checks block and element shape only. It does not enforce which surface a block is allowed on or how many of a block a message can hold, so the skill now checks those against the design principles' surface and limits table instead of treating a passing validation as proof.
  • f063977: Fix create-slack-app offering Pydantic AI when you create a JavaScript agent app. Pydantic AI only works with Python, so the skill now asks for your language first and only lists the AI providers that work with it.
